title: The 4% Rule: How Much Money You Need to Retire 💰 #shorts
description:
In 1994 planner Bill Bengen tested every 30-year period of US market data back to 1926: withdrawing 4% in year one, then raising it with inflation, always lasted at least 30 years. $1M -> $40,000 a year, or yearly spending x 25. In his 2025 book he raised it to 4.7%. It's history, not a guarantee.
Source: W. Bengen, "Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data", Journal of Financial Planning (Oct 1994); Kitces.com and Morningstar summaries; Advisor Perspectives and AAII on "A Richer Retirement" (2025). Education, not financial advice.
script: There's a simple rule that tells you how much money you need to retire.
It's called the four percent rule.
In nineteen ninety-four, a planner named Bill Bengen tested every thirty-year stretch of the US market, back to nineteen twenty-six.
Take out four percent in year one, then just raise it with inflation, and the money lasted at least thirty years. Every single time.
So with one million dollars, you could spend forty thousand a year.
Flip it around. Take your yearly spending, times twenty-five. That's your number.
In twenty twenty-five, Bengen even raised it to four point seven percent. But remember, it's history, not a promise.
